chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Tom Archer's chain of ballrooms in Nebraska and Iowa
summary: Fletcher was bought up for stretches of one-nighters in Tom Archer's string of ballrooms in Mason City, Minneapolis, Des Moines and Omaha.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Fletcher's band, and he was one of the musicians that we talked about that never traveled extensively, in fact had never been on the road on one nighters like Fletcher traveled, you know, doing 35 one nighters in a row, you know, like we played out in Nebraska and all around. There was a chain of ballrooms out in Nebraska during that time. I think you might recall this. There was a guy named Tom Archer that had a lot of ballrooms, like an agency in Mason City, Iowa; in Minneapolis, Minnesota; and Des Moines, Omaha, great, beautiful ballrooms. They were all designed practically the same, and they were gorgeous, huge ballrooms, you know.

Well, Fletcher and Tom Archer were real tight because they knew that Fletcher had a great band. They would always draw in these towns, so he would buy the band up for two or 15 three days or one of those things and play all these ballrooms, you know. Well, Red was a member of Fletcher's band when he played these ballrooms. Of course, it was his maiden trip away from home, and, of course, as you might know, he was in for a baptism.
